notes:
Cartesian Product

  • Ordered pair equality: $(a,b) = (c,d) \iff a=c, b=d$.
  • $A imes B = \{(a,b) : a \in A, b \in B\}$. If $n(A) = p$, $n(B) = q$, then $n(A imes B) = pq$.
  • $A imes B e B imes A$ unless $A = B$ (or one is empty). $A imes (B \cup C) = (A imes B) \cup (A imes C)$.

Relations

  • A relation $R$ from $A$ to $B$ is a subset of $A imes B$. Number of relations from $A$ to $B$ = $2^{n(A)n(B)}$.
  • Domain = set of first elements of ordered pairs actually used; Range = set of second elements; Codomain = the set $B$ itself (Range $\subseteq$ Codomain).

Functions

  • A function $f: A o B$ is a relation where every element of $A$ has exactly one image in $B$. Test: a vertical line cuts the graph at most once.
  • A relation that is not a function has some element of $A$ mapped to two or more elements of $B$, or some element of $A$ with no image.

Identity$f(x)=x$$\mathbb{R}$$\mathbb{R}$

Domain restrictions to check

  • Denominator $ e 0$; expression under an even root $\ge 0$; argument of $\log$ $> 0$.

Algebra of real functions

  • $(f+g)(x) = f(x)+g(x)$; $(fg)(x) = f(x)g(x)$; $(f/g)(x) = f(x)/g(x)$, $g(x) e 0$; $(kf)(x) = kf(x)$. Domain of a combination = intersection of individual domains (also excluding $g(x)=0$ for quotient).

Exam tip

KCET typically asks 1–2 questions from this chapter, mostly on finding domain/range of a given function, identifying whether a relation is a function, and $n(A imes B)$ counting problems. Master domain restrictions (denominator, root, log) — they recur every year.

questions.q: If $n(A) = 3$ and $n(B) = 4$, then $n(A \times B)$ is
questions.explanation: $n(A\times B) = n(A)\cdot n(B) = 3\times4 = 12$.
questions.trick: $n(A\times B) = n(A)\cdot n(B)$ directly.

questions.explanation: Equate components: $x+1=3 \Rightarrow x=2$; $y-2=1 \Rightarrow y=3$.
questions.trick: Ordered pairs equal $\Rightarrow$ match components separately.

questions.q: The total number of relations that can be defined from a set $A$ with 2 elements to a set $B$ with 3 elements is
questions.explanation: Number of relations $= 2^{n(A)n(B)} = 2^{2\times3} = 2^6 = 64$.
questions.trick: Relations from $A$ to $B$ $= 2^{n(A)n(B)}$.

questions.q: If $A = \{1,2\}$ and $B = \{3,4\}$, then $A \times B$ is
questions.explanation: $A\times B$ pairs every element of $A$ (first) with every element of $B$ (second).
questions.trick: $A\times B$: pair every element of $A$ (first) with every $B$ (second).

questions.q: The domain of the real function $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x-5}}$ is
questions.explanation: Need $x - 5 > 0$ (strictly, since it is in the denominator under a root, it cannot be zero), so $x > 5$.
questions.trick: Root's inside $>0$ when it's also in a denominator — strict, not $\ge$.

questions.q: The domain of $f(x) = \sqrt{9-x^2}$ is
questions.explanation: Need $9 - x^2 \ge 0 \Rightarrow x^2 \le 9 \Rightarrow -3 \le x \le 3$.
questions.trick: Even root needs the inside $\ge 0$; solve the resulting inequality.

questions.q: The range of the function $f(x) = \dfrac{x^2}{1+x^2}$ is
questions.explanation: Let $y = x^2/(1+x^2) \Rightarrow x^2 = y/(1-y) \ge 0$, which holds for $0 \le y < 1$ (since $x^2 \ge 0$ and $y=1$ needs $x^2 \to \infty$, never attained).
questions.trick: Let $y=$ the expression, solve for $x^2\ge0$ to bound $y$'s range.

questions.q: Which of the following relations from $A = \{1,2,3\}$ to $B = \{4,5\}$ is NOT a function from $A$ to $B$?
questions.explanation: In option C, $\{(1,4),(1,5),(2,4),(3,5)\}$, the element $1 \in A$ has two images ($4$ and $5$), violating the function definition (unique image for each input).
questions.trick: Function fails if one input maps to two outputs — scan for a repeated first entry.

questions.q: If $f(x) = x^2$ and $g(x) = 2x+1$, then $(f+g)(1)$ equals
questions.trick: $(f+g)(a) = f(a)+g(a)$; evaluate each separately first.

questions.q: The range of the signum function $f(x) = \dfrac{|x|}{x}, x \ne 0$ (and $f(0)=0$) is
questions.explanation: Signum function takes value $1$ for $x>0$, $-1$ for $x<0$, and $0$ at $x=0$.
questions.trick: Signum only ever outputs $-1$, $0$, or $1$.

questions.q: If $A$ has 3 elements and $B$ has 2 elements, the number of ways to choose a relation from $A$ to $B$ that is a function is
questions.explanation: Each of the 3 elements of $A$ independently maps to one of 2 elements of $B$: total functions $= 2^3 = 8$.
questions.trick: Functions $A\to B$ (no restriction) $= n(B)^{n(A)}$.

questions.q: The domain of $f(x) = \log_{10}(x-3)$ is
questions.explanation: Argument of log must be strictly positive: $x - 3 > 0 \Rightarrow x > 3$.
questions.trick: Log domain: argument strictly $>0$.

questions.q: If $f(x) = 2x - 3$ and $g(x) = x+1$, the domain of $(f/g)(x)$ excludes
questions.explanation: $(f/g)(x)$ is undefined where $g(x)=0$, i.e. $x+1=0 \Rightarrow x=-1$.
questions.trick: $(f/g)(x)$ excludes wherever $g(x)=0$.

questions.q: The figure of a relation shows points $(1,2), (1,3), (2,4)$ plotted on a graph. This relation is not a function because
options: it fails the horizontal line test
some element of the domain has more than one image
the range is not a subset of codomain
the domain is not a set
questions.explanation: The vertical line $x=1$ meets the graph at two points ($y=2$ and $y=3$), so $x=1$ has two images — violating the function property.
questions.trick: Vertical line test: two points on one vertical line $\Rightarrow$ not a function.

questions.q: If $R = \{(x,y) : x, y \in \mathbb{Z}, x^2 + y^2 = 25\}$, the domain of $R$ is
questions.explanation: Integer solutions of $x^2+y^2=25$: $(\pm5,0), (0,\pm5), (\pm3,\pm4), (\pm4,\pm3)$. So $x$ takes values $\{-5,-4,-3,0,3,4,5\}$.
questions.trick: List integer $(x,y)$ pairs on the circle, then collect the $x$-values.

questions.q: If $f(x) = x^2 - 1$, then $f(x+1) - f(x)$ equals
questions.trick: Expand $f(x+1)$ and subtract $f(x)$ term by term.

questions.q: If a set $A$ has 3 elements, the number of elements in $A \times A$ is
questions.trick: $n(A\times A) = n(A)^2$.

questions.q: If $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{1-x}$, then $f(f(f(x)))$ equals (for $x \ne 0,1$)
questions.explanation: Check with $x=2$: $f(2) = \dfrac{1}{1-2} = -1$; $f(-1) = \dfrac{1}{1-(-1)} = \dfrac{1}{2}$; $f(1/2) = \dfrac{1}{1-1/2} = 2 = x$. So $f$ has order 3, and $f(f(f(x))) = x$ for all valid $x$.
questions.trick: Try one numeric value through $f$ thrice to spot the cycle back to $x$.

questions.q: The range of $f(x) = [x]$ (greatest integer function) restricted to the domain $[0,3)$ is
questions.trick: $[x]$ is constant on each unit interval $[k,k+1)$ — list those constants.

questions.explanation: The set of first components gives $A=\{1,2\}$ and the set of second components gives $B=\{3,4\}$.
questions.trick: $A =$ set of first coordinates, $B =$ set of second coordinates.

questions.q: The domain of $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{x^2-9}$ is
questions.explanation: $f$ is undefined when $x^2 = 9$, i.e. $x = \pm3$, so the domain excludes both values.
questions.trick: Domain excludes zeros of the denominator — factor and solve.

questions.q: The domain of $f(x) = \sqrt{x^2-4}$ is
questions.explanation: We need $x^2 \ge 4$, which holds for $x \le -2$ or $x \ge 2$.
questions.trick: Even root: need inside $\ge 0$, giving $|x|\ge$ something.

questions.q: The range of the constant function $f(x) = 7$ for all $x \in \mathbb R$ is
questions.explanation: A constant function takes only the single value 7, so its range is $\{7\}$.
questions.trick: Constant function's range is just that single constant.

questions.q: The graph of the identity function $f(x) = x$ is
options: A horizontal line through the origin
A straight line through the origin making $45^\circ$ with the $x$-axis
questions.explanation: $f(x)=x$ gives points like $(1,1),(2,2),\ldots$, which lie on the line $y=x$, at $45^\circ$ to the axes.
questions.trick: $f(x)=x$ plots as the $45^\circ$ line $y=x$ through the origin.

questions.q: If $f(x) = |x|$ (modulus function), then $f(-5) + f(3)$ equals
questions.trick: $|x|$ always strips the sign; add the resulting positives.

questions.q: The value of the greatest integer function $[x]$ at $x = -2.7$ is
questions.explanation: $[x]$ gives the greatest integer less than or equal to $x$; the greatest integer $\le -2.7$ is $-3$.
questions.trick: $[x]$ = greatest integer $\le x$, so round down even for negatives.

questions.q: If $f(x) = x - [x]$ (fractional part function), then $f(3.6)$ equals
questions.trick: Fractional part $= x - [x]$; subtract the floor value.

questions.q: Which of the following functions is even?
questions.explanation: $f(x)=x^2$ satisfies $f(-x)=f(x)$, so it is even; the others are odd or neither.
questions.trick: Even function: $f(-x)=f(x)$ — only even powers of $x$ qualify.

questions.q: Which of the following functions is odd?
questions.explanation: $f(x)=x^3$ satisfies $f(-x) = -f(x)$, so it is odd.
questions.trick: Odd function: $f(-x)=-f(x)$ — pure odd powers of $x$ qualify.

questions.q: The domain of $f(x) = \dfrac{x-2}{x-2}$ is
questions.explanation: Although the expression simplifies to 1, it is undefined at $x=2$ (form $0/0$), so $x=2$ must be excluded from the domain.
questions.trick: Simplifying cancels the factor, but the original zero-denominator point stays excluded.

questions.q: A function $f : A \to B$ associates
options: each element of $A$ with at least one element of $B$
each element of $B$ with exactly one element of $A$
some elements of $A$ with elements of $B$
each element of $A$ with exactly one element of $B$
questions.explanation: By definition, a function assigns to every element of the domain $A$ a unique (exactly one) element of $B$.
questions.trick: Function = exactly one image per domain element, no more, no less.

questions.q: The number of functions that can be defined from a set with 3 elements to a set with 2 elements is
questions.explanation: Each of the 3 elements can map to either of 2 elements, giving $2^3 = 8$ functions.
questions.trick: Total functions $A\to B$ (no restriction) $= n(B)^{n(A)}$.

questions.q: The number of one-one (injective) functions from a set with 3 elements to itself is
questions.explanation: A one-one function from a 3-element set to itself is a permutation of the 3 elements: $3! = 6$.
questions.trick: One-one function from a set to itself = a permutation: $n!$.

questions.q: If $n(A) = 2$ and $n(B) = 3$, the number of relations from $A$ to $B$ is
questions.explanation: A relation from $A$ to $B$ is a subset of $A\times B$, which has $2\times3=6$ elements, giving $2^6 = 64$ relations.
questions.trick: Relations from $A$ to $B$ $= 2^{n(A)n(B)}$.

questions.q: If $f(x) = x^2+1$ and $g(x) = 2x-1$, then $(fg)(2)$ equals
questions.trick: $(fg)(a) = f(a)\cdot g(a)$; multiply the two evaluated values.

questions.q: If $f(x) = x^2$ and $g(x) = \sqrt{x}$ for $x \ge 0$, then $(f \circ g)(x)$ equals
questions.explanation: $(f\circ g)(x) = f(g(x)) = (\sqrt{x})^2 = x$ for $x \ge 0$.
questions.trick: $(f\circ g)(x) = f(g(x))$ — substitute inner into outer.

questions.q: If $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{x}$ for $x \ne 0$, the range of $f$ is
questions.explanation: As $x$ ranges over all nonzero reals, $1/x$ takes every nonzero real value, so the range is $\mathbb R - \{0\}$.
questions.trick: $1/x$ hits every nonzero real as $x$ ranges over nonzero reals.

questions.q: Which of the following relations from $\{1,2,3\}$ to $\{4,5,6,7\}$ IS a function?
questions.explanation: In $\{(1,4),(2,5),(3,4)\}$ every element of the domain $\{1,2,3\}$ appears exactly once; the others either repeat an input with different outputs or miss an input.
questions.trick: Every domain element used exactly once, with no repeats, confirms a function.

questions.q: A curve is such that every vertical line drawn meets it at exactly one point. This curve represents
options: A relation, but never a function
questions.explanation: This is the vertical line test: meeting each vertical line exactly once means each $x$ gives a unique $y$, so the curve is the graph of a function.
questions.trick: Vertical line test passing everywhere = definition of a function.

questions.q: If $n(A)=2$, $n(B)=3$ and $n(C)=4$, the number of elements in $A \times B \times C$ is
questions.explanation: $n(A\times B\times C) = n(A)\cdot n(B)\cdot n(C) = 2\times3\times4 = 24$.
questions.trick: $n(A\times B\times C) = n(A)\,n(B)\,n(C)$.
